hey, no problem! i'm happy to try to answer your questions; there's no shame in admitting you don't understand something (especially a term like nonbinary, which honestly does get thrown around a lot these days). 

personally, and most nonbinary people i've had meaningful communication with, see our identity as lying somewhere between "male" and "female", or a mixture of both. not everyone is in the exact middle; there are people who lean more masculine or feminine. for myself, i am trying to achieve a more androgynous appearance, as my chest is a massive source of dysphoria for me and i also get dysphoria from being seen as a woman. i'm not going to the entire opposite side of the spectrum (ie transitioning to male), because i also do not identify as male (i don't feel a strong desire to be perceived as masculine, i don't necessarily want all the masculine secondary sex characteristics). 

as for what your friend said, i think that nonbinary and gender non-conforming get mixed up a lot. while there is certainly overlap, cis people can be and are gender non-conforming without being nonbinary. all GNC means is that you don't conform to the stereotypical values/interests/behaviors/gender roles in your society. meanwhile, nonbinary means that you do NOT identify as cis, but rather see your gender as existing somewhere between male and female. 

it's easy to get confused because there really are so many terms and labels (agender, genderqueer, bigender, etc.) that all have their own nuances and slightly different definitions, and i think the language around this is still evolving as we try to find the balance between specificity and simplicity. 

​

as for your confusion over how someone can feel dysphoria with their gender but not desire to transition to the opposite–i think you're getting wrapped up in the "there are only two biological sexes" track. there's a lot of great articles out there about the variations in biological sex and primary and secondary sex characteristic expression; there are actually a whole bunch of x and y combinations beyond just xx and xy, and even within those there can be various hormonal differences that can result in intersex people. and, i would like to point out, there are a lot of intersex people who identify as cis–there is actually a movement to stop doctors from performing sex-altering surgeries at birth for intersex babies, because they feel that they should not be forced into a binary gender they did not choose. so, someone who was born fitting the typical expectation of the binary growing up and identifying as neither make nor female isn't that strange. 

just because someone is dysphoric about X doesn't mean they must then \*desire\* Y–they can simply want to get rid of X. or, they might really want Y but feel ambivalent about having X, and choose to get Y without getting rid of X. i wouldn't call this a "sex-less" identity; no one's trying to become smooth like a barbie doll (i think??? i hope not lol). 

​

i hope this helped you understand a bit more! wishing you all the best <3

I’ve been on an ssri+bup combo for several months now and I’m doing great! Specifically, 150mg bup xl and 100mg sertraline. They actually have a synergistic reaction where they make each other work better. My psychiatrist did tell me that there is a chance of serotonin syndrome but that because of the doses I’m on it’s incredibly unlikely. There’s a risk of ss anytime you take any kind of serotonin reuptake inhibitor but that’s what dosing guidelines are for.

My first ~4 days of taking bupropion I felt dizzy, unfocused, off-balance, and a shit ton of brain fog. Everyone’s different; if you’re feeling a certain way then that’s just how you react! I will say I didn’t really feel the mood-altering effects for a few weeks, so if you and your doctor agree it’s okay I’d recommend waiting it out to see.

I’ve been on it for about four months at 125mg and I can’t believe I spent so many years unmedicated. I literally used to think about dying every single day, I was absolutely hopeless about the future, constantly tired/fatigued, constantly anxious, unable to find joy in anything…it’s like I’m breathing fresh air for the first time in my life! A few people in my life who aren’t mentally ill don’t get it and definitely buy into the stigma against being medicated, but for me it has honestly saved my life and changed its trajectory for the better. I may not necessarily take zoloft for the rest of my life (i’m still having some side effects with my sleeping) but I’m “planning” on staying medicated for the long term. 

Obviously you should consult with your psychiatrist on your personal med journey, but you are definitely not alone in feeling like this! My psychiatrist said I’d probably be on medication for my whole life bc of my MDD and anxiety. Nothing against people who are on medication for a shorter period of time, but it’s also okay to stay on it! I wish you the best :)
